setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Argued to be possibly the hottest version ever played; Rousing version, with a lovely transition into Deal closing the first set [11][14]
- **Bertha** (2 reviews): Keith shines; the reviewer rates it above any 1977 Bertha and comparable to early-1970s versions; Jerry gets badly lost; Keith tries to rescue him, but it falls apart [7][10]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Uneven opener, with vocals out of sync at the end [14]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): The final vocal refrain is abandoned in an otherwise decent version [12]
- **Big River** (1 review): Described as blistering [14]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Jerry sings and plays beautifully on this one [7]
- **It Must Have Been The Roses** (1 review): Jerry sounds a bit out of it, though he finishes strongly after the drum break [10]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Around nine minutes in, Weir plays chords from Lost Sailor, which appeared only years later [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-05-10.mtx.dusborne.127408.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 175 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: First set is very upfront and in-your-face, with some tape wear early in Jack Straw; Second set is cleaner with better dynamics, but lacks the U.S. Blues encore [1]
- **gd78-05-10.aud.fishman.18753.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 166 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience tapes on the archive cloudy and not doing the sets justice [8]
- **gd78-05-10.sbd.lai.3899.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 169 min; rated 2/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1978-05-10.127485.aud.moore.berger.flac24**: audience recording; 20 songs; 177 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended the show in person but recalls few specifics about it [10]
- The second set runs almost two hours, and the show was not widely traded, becoming known in the 21st century [12]
- Released as Dick's Picks 25, though that release leaves out the U.S. Blues encore [6]
- Reviewer pairs this show with the following Springfield show as the two shows on Dick's Picks 25 [8]
- Other One, Wharf Rat and Sugar Magnolia called possibly the hottest post-drums stretch in the band's history [11]
- Dick's Picks 25 covers most of this show plus the next night; reviewer thinks this is the better show [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-05-10.mtx.dusborne.127408.flac16**: transferred by Dave Usborne; source: 2 Matrix from Soundboard (shnid:03899) and Audience (shnid:18753) [1]. Also: Recorded on Sony 54-Ps mics into Sony TCD158 cassette; first set from a first-generation cassette, then transferred via EAC to digital [1]
- **gd78-05-10.aud.fishman.18753.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony 54-Ps [5]
- **gd78-05-10.sbd.lai.3899.sbefail.shnf**: source: SBD [2]
- **gd1978-05-10.127485.aud.moore.berger.flac24**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Rob Berger; source: mics uncertain > sony tc-153sd, maxell udxlII's, dolby b [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Veterans Memorial Coliseum - May 10, 1978](https://www.dead.net/show/may-10-1978) [18]
- Poster by Music on TIDAL: [Grateful Dead - Dick's Picks Vol. 25: Veterans Memorial Coliseum, New Haven, CT 5/10/78 / Springfield Civic Center, Spri](https://tidal.com/album/2477548) [19]
